interactionPlan.concept: How horizontal and vertical frequency components combine to determine the orientation and spacing of two-dimensional spatial waves.
learningObjectives: Understand how the frequency parameters u and v independently control the horizontal and vertical wave oscillations.
Explain how the ratio of u and v determines the overall angle and orientation of the 2D wave pattern.
Recognize that higher absolute values of u and v lead to higher spatial frequencies (finer patterns), while negative values change the wave's orientation direction.
Connect the spatial representation of a 2D wave to its representation as a single point in the frequency domain.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: A 2D wave is just the combination of a horizontal wave and a vertical wave; by changing their relative frequencies, you can rotate and scale the pattern to create any spatial grating.

interactions.label: Horizontal u
interactions.effect: Alters the rate of oscillation along the horizontal axis (n), changing the density of vertical stripes.
interactions.teaches: How the u parameter controls the horizontal spatial frequency component.

interactions.label: Vertical v
interactions.effect: Alters the rate of oscillation along the vertical axis (m), tilting the wave pattern vertically.
interactions.teaches: How the v parameter controls the vertical spatial frequency component and how it interacts with u to rotate the wavefronts.

interactions.label: Wave Type
interactions.effect: Switches the underlying mathematical wave function between Sine and Cosine.
interactions.teaches: The phase relationship between sine and cosine waves in 2D space, demonstrating a spatial shift.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: The visualization should consist of two main components placed side-by-side. On the left: a 2D grid plot representing the spatial domain (size 20x20 pixels) where the brightness of each cell (n, m) is determined by the sine or cosine formula using the selected u and v values. Use a high-contrast grayscale colormap (black for minimum value -1, white for maximum value 1). Label the axes 'n' (horizontal) and 'm' (vertical), ranging from 0 to 20. On the right: a 2D coordinate grid representing the frequency domain (u vs v), ranging from -10 to 10 on both axes. Display a prominent colored dot (e.g., bright orange or blue) at the coordinate corresponding to the current (u, v) slider values to visually link the spatial pattern to its 2D spectral coordinate.
